    Essential surjectivity of the primitive restricted Yoneda functor #

    Iyama saturation enlarges the lifted image of a represented boundary cover inside a full-generator representable. The strict-tau homological estimates make that saturated image projective, so the additive Auslander equivalence returns it to a literal factor object.

    The boundary idempotent shows that the boundary cover remains surjective after this replacement. Its weak-cokernel property then identifies the represented factor object with the original poset-space subobject. Consequently the restricted Yoneda image is closed under subobjects and, using the full-support envelope, essentially surjective.
